seoTitle: Padre Pio Story for Kids | Catholic Storybook
seoDescription: Read a child-friendly Padre Pio storybook for ages 5-12 with read-aloud narration, simple language, faith lessons, and an engaging guided experience.
intro: A true story told in simple words: a boy from a small Italian town who learned to pray, became a Capuchin friar, listened to people's sorrows for fifty years, and taught the world to "pray, hope, and don't worry."
shortAnswer: This read-aloud Padre Pio storybook for children ages 5 to 12 tells how Francesco Forgione of Pietrelcina learned to pray, became a Capuchin friar and priest, and spent more than fifty years at San Giovanni Rotondo listening to people's sorrows. It includes his counsel: pray, hope, and don't worry.
summaryHtml:
This read-aloud storybook tells children ages 5 to 12 the true story of Padre Pio: the boy Francesco Forgione from Pietrelcina who learned to pray, became a Capuchin friar and priest, and spent more than fifty years at San Giovanni Rotondo listening to people's sorrows. It tells, gently and honestly, of the wounds he bore, the hospital he built for the sick, and the counsel he left the world: pray, hope, and don't worry.

  • For ages 5 to 12, with read-aloud narration on every page.
  • A 16-page storybook told in simple words.
  • Grounded in the documented record; the fuller adult account is on the St Padre Pio page.
  • Part of the Saint Storybooks library.

faq.a: Children ages 5 to 12, reading on their own or listening with family. Every page has a Read Aloud button with gentle narration, so the book can be heard as well as read.

A Capuchin friar from southern Italy (1887-1968) who heard confessions for up to sixteen hours a day, bore wounds like those of Christ for fifty years, and founded a hospital at San Giovanni Rotondo. The Church canonized him on June 16, 2002.
Yes. It retells documented events of his life. The harder chapters, like the wounds he bore, are told honestly and gently, and the adult page separates what is documented from what is reported.

faq.q: What does "pray, hope, and don't worry" mean?
faq.a: It was Padre Pio's short counsel for anxious people: bring everything to God in prayer, trust Him with the outcome, and refuse to carry tomorrow's fear today.

saintBio.heading: About Saint Padre Pio
saintBio.facts:
Lived
1887-1968
Place
Pietrelcina and San Giovanni Rotondo, Italy
Status
Canonized June 16, 2002, by Pope John Paul II
Feast
September 23
saintBio.body:
Francesco Forgione was born on May 25, 1887 in Pietrelcina, a farming village in southern Italy. At fifteen he entered the Capuchin novitiate and took the name Pio. He was ordained a priest on August 10, 1910. His health was poor, and in 1916 he was sent to San Giovanni Rotondo, where he stayed for the rest of his life.

He heard confessions for many hours a day, and people came from all over Italy and beyond. He founded a hospital, the Casa Sollievo della Sofferenza, and prayer groups that now exist worldwide. He bore the stigmata from September 20, 1918 until his death on September 23, 1968, and his counsel is often quoted: "Pray, hope, and don't worry."

Key teaching

Padre Pio gave his days to prayer, to hearing confessions and to the suffering. The hospital he founded is called the Home for the Relief of Suffering.

cards.title: Prayer First
cards.textHtml: Padre Pio's whole day began and ended with prayer - everything else grew out of it.

cards.title: Listening
cards.textHtml: In the confessional he showed that truly listening to someone is a way of loving them.

cards.title: Patience in Hard Times
cards.textHtml: When he was misunderstood and restricted, he obeyed quietly and kept praying.

cards.title: One Person at a Time
cards.textHtml: He helped whoever stood in front of him - and built a hospital out of other people's pain.

dates.heading: True Dates in the Story
items: May 25, 1887: Birth of Francesco Forgione (Padre Pio) in Pietrelcina, Italy.
1903: He enters the Capuchin novitiate at Morcone and receives the name Pio.
August 10, 1910: He is ordained a priest.
1916: He is assigned to the friary of San Giovanni Rotondo, his home for the rest of his life.
September 20, 1918: He receives the stigmata while praying after Mass.
1956: Casa Sollievo della Sofferenza, the hospital he founded, opens.
September 23, 1968: He dies in his cell at the friary.
May 2, 1999: Beatified by Pope John Paul II.
June 16, 2002: Canonized by Pope John Paul II. His feast day is September 23.
dates.noteHtml: Note: Some well-known details of Padre Pio's life (such as the exact moments of the stigmata) rest on his own letters and witness testimony; the Church investigated his life for decades before canonizing him.
